```python
def tz_localize(self, tz=None, ambiguous='raise', nonexistent='raise'):
    """
    Convert timestamps to local time.

    Localize a datetime series by converting UTC times represented in the
    data to local time using `tz`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tz : str or pytz.tzinfo.TZInfo, optional
        Time zone name for which to retrieve the localuted
        datetime. This should normally be an IANA standard time zone
        database name. If it is None, then `None` will be returned.
        Defaults to None.

    ambiguous : {'raise', 'infer'}, default='raise'
        How to handle ambiguous times at a daylight saving time
        crossover. infer: use the first occurrence to infer what the rest
        of the day should be.

    nonexistent : {'raise', 'NaT', 'shift_forward', 'shift_backward'}
                  or timedelta, default 'raise'
        If ``'raise'``, an exception will be raised if a non-existent time is
        encountered.
        If ``'NaT'``, the time will be replaced by NaT.
        If ``'shift_forward'``, the clock will jump forward one hour,
        shifting all times back accordingly.
        If ``'shift_backward'``, the clock will jump backward one hour,
        shifting all times forward accordingly.

    Returns
    -------
    localized : Timestamp or Series of Timestamps
        The localized datetime object.
    """
```

This function converts UTC times represented in the data to local time using `tz`. It also handles ambiguous times at daylight saving time crossovers and non-existent times according to the specified parameters.
